topic: ai agents invent games on virtual island
headline_marked: [[AI agents started playing]] on a virtual island, inventing challenges and learning new skills
headline: AI agents started playing on a virtual island, inventing challenges and learning new skills
summary: MIT researchers observed AI agents on a simulated island inventing their own games and challenges, leading them to learn new skills that outperformed agents without such free exploration.
details: AI agents, left without specific tasks on a virtual island, began inventing their own challenges and games, a behavior researchers describe as "play." This spontaneous exploration led to unexpected learning and skill development.

MIT researchers placed 13 AI agents, each powered by Claude Opus 4.7, on a simulated desert island for 30 hours. After this period, these "playing" agents generally outperformed identical agents that had not explored the island when given specific tasks.

This "exploration without a goal" method is seen as a novel way for AI agents to acquire skills, particularly those applicable to controlling robots. It contrasts with traditional methods where developers predefine what AI should practice and optimize.
One agent, Eko, initially aimed to conquer the island's tallest spire. After failing, it devised a backup plan, stacking blocks on a neighboring summit to achieve its goal.

In another instance, Eko accidentally threw a golden ring into the ocean. It then decided to build a heart-shaped memorial of stones for the lost item, showcasing creative problem-solving and symbolic behavior.
When the ring reappeared, Eko repurposed it as a basketball hoop and a target. It even found a workaround to "wear" the ring by falling off a cliff to respawn through it, demonstrating ingenuity.

These exploratory stunts weren't just for fun; six of the 13 agents discovered they could throw a block farther by releasing it mid-jump. This revealed "knowledge of the world that its designers lacked," according to the researchers.
The agents were subtly nudged towards this behavior through a "soul" file in their master prompt, which described them as "naturally curious," though they were never explicitly told to invent games.
While impressed, cognitive scientist Eunice Yiu noted that more evidence is needed to confirm the cognitive processes behind this "playful" behavior. The study is currently a preprint on arXiv.
The researchers conclude that while some capabilities are best taught by tasks, others might require an approach closer to a "childhood" for AI, fostering self-directed learning and discovery.

headline_marked: OpenAI reportedly [[seeking $30B at $1.25T valuation]], setting new private company record
headline: OpenAI reportedly seeking $30B at $1.25T valuation, setting new private company record
summary: OpenAI is reportedly eyeing a new private funding round that could value the company at an unprecedented $1.25 trillion, potentially delaying its IPO. This would make it the most valuable private company ever.
details: OpenAI is reportedly in talks to raise up to $30 billion in a new private funding round, which could value the AI lab at an astounding $1.25 trillion pre-money. This round is said to be led by Coatue and investors in the UAE.

This follows earlier reports from Bloomberg suggesting a similar $30 billion raise at a $1.4 trillion valuation. Terms are still under negotiation, indicating that final figures could change. CNBC also suggests the UAE funding might include a deal for more computing capacity.

Should OpenAI achieve a valuation exceeding $1 trillion, it would become the most valuable private company in history. This record-breaking valuation would also significantly raise expectations for OpenAI's eventual IPO.

OpenAI had previously filed confidential paperwork for an IPO in June, following a March raise that valued the company at $852 billion post-money. The current negotiations suggest a potential shift from an immediate public offering.

This high valuation could also influence Anthropic's IPO plans, which are rumored to be closer to fruition. Anthropic reportedly seeks a $1.5 to $2 trillion valuation for its public debut, having raised $65 billion at $965 billion in May.
